Validation of the electability threshold and comparison of the candidates placed within and just below it in the general election of July 2023 (sex, occupation, previous party, candidacies in 2013-2017).

```{r SETUP}
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(sf)
library(rnaturalearth)
library(httr2)
library(countrycode)
library(mapSpain)
library(stargazer)
library(rvest)
library(here)

# tables are printed as text here; use type = "html" (or "latex") for the written document
table_type <- "text"

# objects made by 02_data_extraction.qmd
```

# Regressions

```{r EXPECTED SEATS VARIABLE AS A PREDICTOR}
library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)
library(broom)

# ---- 1. one row per VOX list (election + chamber + constituency) ----------------------
expected_check <- vox_candidates |>
  filter(is_titular %in% c(TRUE, NA)) |>
  group_by(level, election, chamber, province, expected_seats, expected_seats_source) |>
  summarise(seats = sum(is_elected %in% TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(from_cis = expected_seats_source == "CIS constituency estimate")

expected_check |> count(level, expected_seats_source)

# ---- 2. do the expected seats predict the seats actually won? --------------------------
# standard errors clustered by election: constituencies of the same election share shocks
models <- list(
  "1 Pooled"      = lm(seats ~ expected_seats, data = expected_check),
  "2 + level FE"  = lm(seats ~ expected_seats + level, data = expected_check),
  "3 + source"    = lm(seats ~ expected_seats * from_cis + level, data = expected_check),
  "4 National"    = lm(seats ~ expected_seats, data = filter(expected_check, level == "National")),
  "5 Autonomical" = lm(seats ~ expected_seats, data = filter(expected_check, level == "Autonomical")),
  "6 Municipal"   = lm(seats ~ expected_seats, data = filter(expected_check, level == "Municipal"))
)

regression_table <- list()
for (m in names(models)) {
  regression_table[[m]] <- coeftest(models[[m]],
                                    vcov = vcovCL(models[[m]], cluster = ~ election)) |>
    tidy() |>
    mutate(model = m,
           n     = nobs(models[[m]]),
           r2    = summary(models[[m]])$r.squared)
}
regression_table <- bind_rows(regression_table) |>
  select(model, term, estimate, std.error, p.value, n, r2) |>
  mutate(across(c(estimate, std.error, r2), \(x) round(x, 3)),
         p.value = signif(p.value, 3))

regression_table |> print(n = Inf)

# ---- 3. the threshold: are the top_expected candidates the ones who got elected? --------
electable_check <- vox_candidates |>
  filter(is_titular %in% c(TRUE, NA)) |>
  mutate(is_elected = is_elected %in% TRUE)

electable_logit <- glm(is_elected ~ top_expected + level,
                       family = binomial, data = electable_check)

coeftest(electable_logit, vcov = vcovCL(electable_logit, cluster = ~ election)) |>
  tidy() |>
  mutate(odds_ratio = exp(estimate))

# share elected among top_expected and the rest
electable_check |>
  group_by(level, top_expected) |>
  summarise(candidates = n(), elected = sum(is_elected),
            share_elected = mean(is_elected), .groups = "drop")

# ---- 4. plot: expected seats against seats won -------------------------------------------
ggplot(expected_check, aes(expected_seats, seats)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_jitter(aes(colour = expected_seats_source), width = 0.1, height = 0.1, alpha = 0.5, size = 1.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ level, scales = "free") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("CIS constituency estimate"          = "#0072B2",
                                 "previous result, same constituency" = "#E69F00",
                                 "no CIS estimate before 2018 (0)"    = "#CC79A7",
                                 "first contest (0)"                  = "#999999")) +
  labs(x = "Expected seats", y = "Seats actually won", colour = NULL,
       title = "Do the expected seats predict the seats Vox actually won?",
       subtitle = "One point per list. Dashed line: perfect prediction.") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

```{r REGRESSION SEX}
library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)
library(broom)
library(survival)

# Who gets an electable place? The Congress candidates of July 2023 are split in two
# groups by data/manual/isco_candidatos_2023.xlsx (isco08_group): those within the electoral
# threshold of their constituency ("Dentro del umbral", the heads of list included) and
# the three titulars right below it ("Justo debajo del umbral"), who are neither heads
# of list nor above the threshold in that election. One row per person
threshold_sample <- vox_candidates |>
  filter(election == "general_2023_07", chamber == "Congress",
         is_titular %in% c(TRUE, NA), !is.na(isco08_group)) |>
  slice_min(list_position, n = 1, by = person_id, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  mutate(electable      = isco08_group == "Dentro del umbral",
         sex            = factor(sex, levels = c("Male", "Female")),
         isco_class     = case_when(isco08_major == "1"  ~ "1 Managers",
                                    isco08_major == "2"  ~ "2 Professionals",
                                    !is.na(isco08_major) ~ "3 Rest",
                                    TRUE                 ~ "4 Unknown") |>
                            factor(levels = c("3 Rest", "1 Managers", "2 Professionals", "4 Unknown")),
         prev_party_any = has_prev_party %in% TRUE) |>
  select(person_id, candidate, province, list_position, electable, isco08_group, sex,
         isco08, isco08_title, isco08_major, isco08_major_title, isco_class,
         prev_party, prev_party_any, in_lists_2013_2017)

threshold_sample |> count(isco08_group, electable)

# the constituencies that identify the comparison: those with people in both groups
threshold_sample |>
  summarise(within = sum(electable), below = sum(!electable), .by = province) |>
  arrange(desc(within)) |>
  print(n = Inf)

# ---- 1. sex: descriptives and Fisher exact test ----------------------------------------
sex_table <- table(sex = threshold_sample$sex, electable = threshold_sample$electable)
sex_table
prop.table(sex_table, margin = 1) |> round(3)
fisher.test(sex_table)

# ---- 2. sex as a predictor of an electable place ----------------------------------------
# the odds of an electable place are compared in two ways:
#   a. a logit over the whole sample, standard errors clustered by constituency
#   b. a conditional logit, which compares the candidates of the same constituency only
#      (constituencies with no electable candidate drop out of this model)
# list_position is not a control here: the two groups are defined by it
threshold_models <- list(
  "1 Logit"             = glm(electable ~ sex, family = binomial, data = threshold_sample),
  "2 Conditional logit" = clogit(electable ~ sex + strata(province), data = threshold_sample)
)

# the table of every model: clustered standard errors for the logits, the model's own for
# the conditional logit, which is already within constituency
threshold_table <- list()
for (m in names(threshold_models)) {
  threshold_table[[m]] <- (if (inherits(threshold_models[[m]], "coxph"))
                             tidy(threshold_models[[m]])
                           else
                             coeftest(threshold_models[[m]],
                                      vcov = vcovCL(threshold_models[[m]], cluster = ~ province)) |>
                               tidy()) |>
    mutate(model = m, n = nobs(threshold_models[[m]]))
}
threshold_table <- bind_rows(threshold_table) |>
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
  mutate(odds_ratio = exp(estimate)) |>
  select(model, term, estimate, std.error, odds_ratio, p.value, n) |>
  mutate(across(c(estimate, std.error, odds_ratio), \(x) round(x, 3)),
         p.value = signif(p.value, 3))

threshold_table |> print(n = Inf)
```

```{r REGRESSION ISCO + SEX}
# The occupation before politics (ISCO-08 major group) added to sex. The four digit codes
# are collapsed into managers (1), professionals (2), the rest (3-9) and "Unknown", the
# candidates whose occupation was not found: they are 2 of the 44 within the threshold and
# 61 of the 137 below it, so the category also measures how much press each group gets
threshold_sample |> count(electable, isco_class)
threshold_sample |> count(electable, isco08_major, isco08_major_title) |> print(n = Inf)

isco_table <- table(isco = threshold_sample$isco_class, electable = threshold_sample$electable)
isco_table
prop.table(isco_table, margin = 1) |> round(3)
fisher.test(isco_table)

# the same, dropping the candidates without a known occupation
fisher.test(isco_table[rownames(isco_table) != "4 Unknown", ])

threshold_models <- list(
  "1 Logit, ISCO"            = glm(electable ~ isco_class, family = binomial, data = threshold_sample),
  "2 Logit, ISCO + sex"      = glm(electable ~ isco_class + sex, family = binomial, data = threshold_sample),
  "3 Conditional logit"      = clogit(electable ~ isco_class + sex + strata(province), data = threshold_sample),
  "4 Logit, ISCO known only" = glm(electable ~ isco_class + sex, family = binomial,
                                   data = filter(threshold_sample, isco_class != "4 Unknown"))
)

threshold_table <- list()
for (m in names(threshold_models)) {
  threshold_table[[m]] <- (if (inherits(threshold_models[[m]], "coxph"))
                             tidy(threshold_models[[m]])
                           else
                             coeftest(threshold_models[[m]],
                                      vcov = vcovCL(threshold_models[[m]], cluster = ~ province)) |>
                               tidy()) |>
    mutate(model = m, n = nobs(threshold_models[[m]]))
}
threshold_table <- bind_rows(threshold_table) |>
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
  mutate(odds_ratio = exp(estimate)) |>
  select(model, term, estimate, std.error, odds_ratio, p.value, n) |>
  mutate(across(c(estimate, std.error, odds_ratio), \(x) round(x, 3)),
         p.value = signif(p.value, 3))

threshold_table |> print(n = Inf)
```

```{r REGRESSION ISCO + SEX + PREV_PARTY}
# A previous party added to the occupation and sex. has_prev_party is TRUE or NA, because
# the absence of a previous party cannot be told apart from the absence of evidence of one;
# to compare the two groups every NA is read here as FALSE (prev_party_any, built with the
# sample), so the coefficient is the effect of a previous party *on record*
threshold_sample |> count(electable, prev_party_any)
threshold_sample |> filter(prev_party_any) |> count(electable, prev_party) |> print(n = Inf)

party_table <- table(prev_party = threshold_sample$prev_party_any, electable = threshold_sample$electable)
party_table
prop.table(party_table, margin = 1) |> round(3)
fisher.test(party_table)

threshold_models <- list(
  "1 Logit, party"              = glm(electable ~ prev_party_any, family = binomial, data = threshold_sample),
  "2 Logit, ISCO + sex + party" = glm(electable ~ isco_class + sex + prev_party_any,
                                      family = binomial, data = threshold_sample),
  "3 Conditional logit"         = clogit(electable ~ isco_class + sex + prev_party_any + strata(province),
                                         data = threshold_sample),
  "4 + lists of 2013-2017"      = glm(electable ~ isco_class + sex + prev_party_any + in_lists_2013_2017,
                                      family = binomial, data = threshold_sample)
)

threshold_table <- list()
for (m in names(threshold_models)) {
  threshold_table[[m]] <- (if (inherits(threshold_models[[m]], "coxph"))
                             tidy(threshold_models[[m]])
                           else
                             coeftest(threshold_models[[m]],
                                      vcov = vcovCL(threshold_models[[m]], cluster = ~ province)) |>
                               tidy()) |>
    mutate(model = m, n = nobs(threshold_models[[m]]))
}
threshold_table <- bind_rows(threshold_table) |>
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
  mutate(odds_ratio = exp(estimate)) |>
  select(model, term, estimate, std.error, odds_ratio, p.value, n) |>
  mutate(across(c(estimate, std.error, odds_ratio), \(x) round(x, 3)),
         p.value = signif(p.value, 3))

threshold_table |> print(n = Inf)

# an odds ratio in the thousands with a huge standard error means a category has no
# variation left (complete separation): read the Fisher tables above instead
```

# Tables for the text

```{r TABLE OF RQ2 DESCRIPTIVES}
# profile of the two groups, with the Fisher exact test of each variable. Previous parties:
# PP includes Alianza Popular; the historical far right follows the abbreviations of
# 02_data_extraction.qmd (Fuerza Nueva, Falange, Democracia Nacional, Juntas Españolas...)
far_right_abbreviations <- "\\b(FN|FE-JONS|LF|FEA|DN|JJEE|AES|E-2000|PxC|MSR|ADN)\\b"

rq2_sample <- threshold_sample |>
  mutate(group         = if_else(electable, "Within the threshold", "Just below it"),
         female        = sex == "Female",
         managers      = isco_class == "1 Managers",
         professionals = isco_class == "2 Professionals",
         other_isco    = isco_class == "3 Rest",
         unknown_isco  = isco_class == "4 Unknown",
         prev_pp       = str_detect(replace_na(prev_party, ""), "\\b(PP|AP)\\b"),
         prev_cs       = str_detect(replace_na(prev_party, ""), "\\bCs\\b"),
         prev_far      = str_detect(replace_na(prev_party, ""), far_right_abbreviations))

rq2_variables <- c("Women"                                    = "female",
                   "Managers (ISCO 1)"                        = "managers",
                   "Professionals (ISCO 2)"                   = "professionals",
                   "Other occupations (ISCO 3-9)"             = "other_isco",
                   "Occupation unknown"                       = "unknown_isco",
                   "Stood for another party before"           = "prev_party_any",
                   "   of which PP or AP"                     = "prev_pp",
                   "   of which Cs"                           = "prev_cs",
                   "   of which historical far right"         = "prev_far",
                   "On a Vox list in 2013-2017"               = "in_lists_2013_2017")

rq2_descriptives <- tibble(Variable = names(rq2_variables), variable = unname(rq2_variables)) |>
  mutate(within = map_chr(variable, \(v) {
           x <- rq2_sample[[v]][rq2_sample$electable]
           str_c(sum(x), " (", format(round(100 * mean(x), 1), nsmall = 1), "%)")
         }),
         below = map_chr(variable, \(v) {
           x <- rq2_sample[[v]][!rq2_sample$electable]
           str_c(sum(x), " (", format(round(100 * mean(x), 1), nsmall = 1), "%)")
         }),
         fisher_p = map_dbl(variable, \(v) fisher.test(table(rq2_sample[[v]], rq2_sample$electable))$p.value),
         fisher_p = if_else(fisher_p < 0.001, "<0.001", format(round(fisher_p, 3), nsmall = 3))) |>
  select(-variable) |>
  add_row(Variable = "Candidates", within = as.character(sum(rq2_sample$electable)),
          below = as.character(sum(!rq2_sample$electable)), fisher_p = "", .before = 1) |>
  rename(`Within the threshold` = within, `Just below it` = below, `Fisher p` = fisher_p)

stargazer(as.data.frame(rq2_descriptives), summary = FALSE, rownames = FALSE, type = table_type,
          title = "Candidates within and just below the electability threshold, Congress, July 2023",
          notes = c("Number of candidates and share of each group. Fisher: exact test of the variable against the group.",
                    "A candidate can have stood for several parties."))
```

```{r TABLE OF RQ2 REGRESSIONS}
# the logits of the text in one table: odds ratios, with 95% confidence intervals from
# standard errors clustered by constituency (the model's own for the conditional logit)
rq2_models <- list(
  glm(electable ~ sex, family = binomial, data = threshold_sample),
  glm(electable ~ isco_class + sex, family = binomial, data = threshold_sample),
  glm(electable ~ isco_class + sex + prev_party_any, family = binomial, data = threshold_sample),
  glm(electable ~ isco_class + sex + prev_party_any + in_lists_2013_2017,
      family = binomial, data = threshold_sample),
  clogit(electable ~ isco_class + sex + prev_party_any + in_lists_2013_2017 + strata(province),
         data = threshold_sample)
)

rq2_vcov <- map(rq2_models, \(m) if (inherits(m, "coxph")) vcov(m) else vcovCL(m, cluster = ~ province))
rq2_se   <- map(rq2_vcov, \(v) sqrt(diag(v)))
rq2_or   <- map(rq2_models, \(m) exp(coef(m)))
rq2_ci   <- map2(rq2_models, rq2_se, \(m, se) exp(cbind(coef(m) - 1.96 * se, coef(m) + 1.96 * se)))
rq2_p    <- map2(rq2_models, rq2_se, \(m, se) 2 * pnorm(-abs(coef(m) / se)))

stargazer(rq2_models, type = table_type,
          coef = rq2_or, ci.custom = rq2_ci, p = rq2_p, t.auto = FALSE, p.auto = FALSE,
          omit = "Constant", digits = 2,
          title = "Odds of an electable position, Congress candidates of July 2023",
          dep.var.caption = "Placed within the electability threshold", dep.var.labels.include = FALSE,
          column.labels = c("Logit", "Logit", "Logit", "Logit", "Conditional logit"),
          model.names = FALSE,
          covariate.labels = c("Managers (ISCO 1)", "Professionals (ISCO 2)", "Occupation unknown",
                               "Female", "Stood for another party before", "On a Vox list in 2013-2017"),
          omit.stat = c("aic", "ll", "rsq", "max.rsq", "wald", "lr", "logrank"),
          notes.append = FALSE,
          notes = c("Odds ratios; 95% confidence intervals in brackets, from standard errors clustered by",
                    "constituency (logits). The conditional logit compares candidates of the same constituency.",
                    "Reference: men, occupations of ISCO groups 3-9. * p<0.1; ** p<0.05; *** p<0.01"))
```
